def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers_list = instance["customer_ids"]
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    n_hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", None)

    customers = list(customers_list)
    if not customers:
        return []

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            c += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return c

    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for v in route:
            s += demands[v]
        return s

    # Initial solution: deterministic Clarke-Wright savings merge from singleton routes
    # Each customer starts as its own route: [i]
    routes = [[v] for v in customers]
    load = [demands[v] for v in customers]
    node_to_rid = {}
    head = {}
    tail = {}
    for rid, r in enumerate(routes):
        v = r[0]
        node_to_rid[v] = rid
        head[rid] = v
        tail[rid] = v

    # Compute savings for all unordered pairs (i, j)
    # savings(i,j) = d(depot,i)+d(depot,j)-d(i,j)
    savings = []
    m = len(customers)
    for a in range(m):
        i = customers[a]
        di = matrix[depot][i]
        for b in range(a + 1, m):
            j = customers[b]
            s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    # Deterministic sort: by savings desc, then i asc, then j asc
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[2]))

    alive = [True] * len(routes)
    # Merge greedily while feasible: only endpoint merges, with possible route reversal to align
    for s, i, j in savings:
        if not alive[node_to_rid[i]] or not alive[node_to_rid[j]]:
            continue
        ri = node_to_rid[i]
        rj = node_to_rid[j]
        if ri == rj:
            continue
        # Try i tail + j head
        can1 = (tail[ri] == i and head[rj] == j and load[ri] + load[rj] <= capacity)
        # Try j tail + i head (merge rj + ri)
        can2 = (tail[rj] == j and head[ri] == i and load[ri] + load[rj] <= capacity)
        if can1 or can2:
            if can1:
                new_route = routes[ri] + routes[rj]
            else:
                new_route = routes[rj] + routes[ri]
            routes[ri] = new_route
            load[ri] = load[ri] + load[rj]
            alive[rj] = False
            # Update head/tail and node_to_rid for nodes in rj
            head[ri] = new_route[0]
            tail[ri] = new_route[-1]
            for v in routes[rj]:
                node_to_rid[v] = ri
            # Mark head/tail for rj unused
            # (No need to clear since alive[rj]=False)
        # Optional conservative stopping if many vehicles are already enough; but keep deterministic.
        if n_hint is not None:
